description: Square four-post pergola module with a flat open roof of evenly spaced bamboo slats on paired beams, open on all sides and casting a striped shade.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square four-post pergola module with a flat open roof of evenly spaced bamboo slats laid across paired beams, four square timber posts at the corners, open on all sides Materials: Honey-toned bamboo slats faded unevenly to grey on the sun side, fine longitudinal fibre grain and node banding, dark timber posts with checking splits and old bolt stains bleeding rust.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 1,416/4,000 triangles, 2/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. Turntable passes with NO --allow-holes.

featureReviews.evidence: Measured bounds -2.000..2.000 in x and z and 0.000..2.600 in y -- the declared 4.00 x 2.60 x 4.00 exactly, with nothing crossing the cell edge. The POST owns +-2.000 and the beam and cap rail step back 10 mm and 5 mm behind it, so the post head reads as a joint and check-coplanar is clean at 0.001 m. Turntable silhouette ratios 0.990 / 0.999 / 0.990 against azimuth 0.
featureReviews.notes: The height is the module contract, not the plate: the Meshy proxy reads w:h:d 1 : 0.83 : 1.00 and the built bay is 1 : 0.65 : 1.00, a mean divergence of 0.334 of the height. The registry notes fix a flat 2.60 m roof on a 4 m grid because a player walks under it and because the grid divides the kit's 8 m tiles 2 x 2. The proxy IS used for the plan and confirms it square on all ten bands.

featureReviews.evidence: Forty-eight round 70 mm culms at a 79.2 mm pitch with a 9.2 mm gap, MERGED rather than instanced so each carries its own uv phase, roll, radius, height and a different tone at each end. Node rings land at 300 mm on every culm and at a different station on each of the forty-eight. The turntable now passes with NO --allow-holes: enclosed-background fraction 0.000 at azimuth 0 and 180 and 0.008 at 90 and 270 against the 0.010 threshold, largest hole 41 px.
featureReviews.notes: Culm DIAMETER is the one number not taken from the plate: scaled against its own frame the plate's culms come to about 190 mm at a 4 m bay, which is not a bamboo that exists. What is taken from the plate is its gap-to-pitch ratio of 0.12. The plate's staggered butt joints along each culm are carried as a two-tone gradient rather than as geometry.

featureReviews.evidence: Three timber tones where the first build had one: post #5c4b3a, cap rail #87715c, beam #977f66, measured back at 51 / 89 / 105 against the plate's 54 / 94 / 111. Grain runs ALONG every member because u follows each member's own length axis, on a 1.80 m tile with a per-member (u, v) phase. Checking splits and rust bleed on a 512 px multiply canvas.
featureReviews.notes: The first build lifted the whole frame to one brown at luma 115 for fear of the background test and recorded that as its largest deliberate departure from measurement. It was unnecessary: the test is `distance > 24 from the backdrop OR (saturation > 0.16 and luma < 0.94)`, so it is CHROMA that carries a dark timber. The post ships at a rendered luma of 46-51 with saturation 0.355 and the gate reads it as foreground on both clauses.

name: Bamboo Slat Pergola Module
nameTh: ซุ้มระแนงไม้ไผ่
notes: One bay of a modular outdoor roof kit: 4 x 4 m footprint on a 4 m grid, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2, so a canopy grid lands on the paving grid. Four corner posts, because the brief is a module that includes its own poles and must therefore stand alone; placed side by side the posts pair up at the shared edges, which is what a real market row looks like rather than a defect to design out. Flat at 2.6 m. This is the one module in the set that does NOT close its roof: the slats are spaced, so it casts a striped shade and the sky shows through, which is the whole point of a pergola and is also why it cannot be authored as a textured deck with an alpha cutout -- an alpha roof seen from underneath at a grazing angle is a row of hard edges, and the slats have real depth a player sees from below. Model the slats as one repeated element and expect this module to sit nearer its draw-call and triangle ceilings than the others in the set. Open on all sides, no climbing plants -- vegetation is its own category and a separate prop.
